common_name: Neotropical Rainforest Sophophora Fly (Sex-Comb Loss & High Inversion Polymorphism)
scale_statement: 1.5 µm detail scale at geological age 0 Ma

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila willistoni (1.5 µm, detail scale)

governing_model.name: Schnakenberg two-species reaction-diffusion
equations: du/dt = Du * laplacian(u) + gamma * (a - u + u^2 v)
dv/dt = Dv * laplacian(v) + gamma * (b - u^2 v)
governing_model.selected_wavelength: lambda_max = 2*pi / k_max, where k_max = argmax sigma(k) and sigma is the larger Jacobian eigenvalue of J - k^2 D
governing_model.boundary_condition: Periodic on a cuticle patch whose side is an integer number of selected wavelengths. No-flux (Neumann) is the biological cell boundary; the periodic patch is the repeating granule lattice inside the cell.
governing_model.calibration_note: a, b, gamma and the diffusivity ratio are a reconstruction. They are constrained so the fastest-growing mode equals the assigned 1.466 µm scale. They are not measurements from a willistoni biochemical table, and they are not the cellular-tier sibling parameters alpha_scale=1.63, beta_offset=0.38.

chronospecies.lineage_note: Subgenus Drosophila, large sap-flux fly. Not a literal ancestor; the catalog chronoseries predecessor at this slot.
Sophophora obscura & willistoni clade. Sex-comb loss and high inversion polymorphism mark the lineage and do not enter k_c.
melanogaster-subgroup successor in the catalog chronoseries. Abdominal yellow/tan gradation is a larger-scale cis-regulatory phenotype (Jeong et al. 2008).

what_changes_at_this_scale.changes: Absolute Du and Dv scale as lambda^2, and lambda scales as body_length^0.35. Cell diameter scales linearly with body length, so granules per cell (cell_diameter / lambda) fall from virilis to yakuba to willistoni.
what_changes_at_this_scale.not_the_sibling_slot: Slot 2931 is the 86 µm cellular tergite mode. This slot is the 1.5 µm intra-cellular granule mode.

specimen.description: Drosophila willistoni female, lateral view, light-blue background
